text:
Every (episode, follower) pair is covered, so there are no misses. The plan uses four paid periods: 1549 + 1099 + 2 × 1399 = 5446 cents ($54.46).

**Concurrency limit (3 services)**
- From Nov 1 to Nov 12, already-paid access alone fills or exceeds the limit. Nov 1–7 has four services and Nov 8–12 has three. So no new period can give access before Nov 13.
- From Nov 13 to Nov 24 only Marquee and Northline are on, so one more service fits. From Nov 29 nothing is already paid.

**Velvet Lantern (Northline, leaving, Wen and Dana)**
- Its window is Nov 1–13, and Northline is already paid until Nov 25. No purchase is needed.

**The Velvet Orchard (Lumen, Dana, 30 days)**
- Episode 1 (Nov 5) is covered by the existing access, which ends Nov 8.
- Episodes 2–7 need access on some day in Nov 12–Dec 12 and some day in Dec 17–Jan 16.
- Any single period starting between Nov 18 and Dec 12 does both. I chose **Lumen from Dec 1** (access Dec 1–Dec 31).

**The Copper Orchard (Orbit, Dana)**
- All episodes drop Dec 6, so Dana's window is Dec 6–Jan 5. **Orbit from Dec 6** covers it.

**Marquee shows**
- The Velvet Archive (Wen, 14 days) episodes 1–3 are covered by the existing access, which ends Nov 29. Episodes 4–7 need a period starting between Dec 18 and Dec 19.
- The Amber Orchard (Dana, 30 days) has 12 weekly episodes from Jan 3 to Mar 21.
- **Marquee from Dec 19** gives access Dec 19–Jan 18. That covers Velvet Archive episodes 4–7 and Amber Orchard episodes 1–3.
- **Marquee from Feb 23** gives access Feb 23–Mar 22. That covers Amber Orchard episodes 4–12. Episode 4's window ends Feb 23, and episode 12 releases Mar 21.
- So two Marquee periods cover both shows.

At most three services have access on any day: Lumen, Orbit and Marquee overlap in December.

